data.title: Worker dormitory rents rise 2.1% in H1
data.description:
Average bed rents rose to $495 per bed/month.

Singapore’s Class 4 worker dormitory bed rents rose 2.1% to $495 per bed per month in the first half (H1) of 2026, driven by demand from the construction, marine shipyard, and process industries. 

According to a joint report by the Dormitory Association of Singapore Limited and Knight Frank Singapore, there were 60 Class 4 dormitories in Singapore as at H1 2026, offering 287,837 beds and making up 61.6% of the islandwide bed load. 

The total bed inventory grew 6.3% year-on-year, with 13,910 new Class 4 beds added between H1 2025 and H1 2026. Of these, NESST Tukang Dormitory (2,400 beds), Westlite Toh Guan (1,764 beds), and Westlite Mandai (3,696 beds) contributed a combined 7,860 new beds.

Occupancy pressure eased, with average islandwide occupancy declining 1.3 percentage points to 95.8% from 97.1% in H2 2025. The east zone saw the largest drop, falling 4.6 percentage points to 93.7%, while the central zone declined to 93.6%. The west zone recorded 98.3% occupancy, down from 99.0% six months earlier.

Average bed rents increased across all zones: up 1.9% to S$525 in the east, 2.9% to $535 in the central, and 4.5% to $460 in the west. Monthly bed rents have grown 83.3% since H1 2019, when they were $270. The report noted that the completion of NESST Tukang Dormitory, which fully complies with the New Dormitory Standards (NDS), likely contributed to the upward pull in the west zone’s average rent.

Government land tenders in 2026 saw higher land rates for new dormitory sites. S11 Ascendene Management won the Terusan Edge parcel for $105m ($32,812 per bed), whilst Centurion Corporation subsidiaries secured Kranji Close for $343m ($49,000 per bed) and Lok Yang Way for $221.7m ($44,333 per bed). The report said these rates are substantially higher than the $24,364 per bed awarded at Ubi Avenue 3 in January 2023. The Dormitory Transition Scheme, with its 2030 deadline, and the NDS scheme are expected to tighten supply and raise bed rents further.

These awarded sites, along with others, are expected to add around 40,200 beds before 2030, with at least six more purpose-built dormitories totalling about 47,000 beds in the pipeline, according to the Ministry of Manpower.

“Bed rents can be expected to increase by around 5% for the whole of 2026 after having risen 2.1% in the first half of the year,” said Leonard Tay, Head, Research, Knight Frank Singapore.

data.title: HK Mineral Boutique owner not part of DNA Brands probe, Singapore watchdog says
data.description:
The CCS refund scheme covers Singapore outlets run by DNA Brands. 

The Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCS) has clarified that The Mineral Boutique Limited in Hong Kong was not subject to its investigation into DNA Brands Co Pte Ltd.

The watchdog said in an update dated 11 August that references to The Mineral Boutique concerned specific Singapore outlets operated by DNA Brands under The Mineral Boutique name.

The Mineral Boutique Limited is the Hong Kong-registered owner of The Mineral Boutique brand and trademarks.

CCS had earlier secured a commitment of up to $1m in refunds for consumers affected by unfair sales practices at beauty and wellness outlets operated by DNA Brands.

The watchdog’s investigation found that an area manager and certain employees had used coordinated pressure tactics since 2023 to induce customers into unintended purchases.

The Singapore outlets identified under CCS’ refund scheme include locations at Jewel Changi Airport, NEX and Wheelock Place, which were operated by DNA Brands.

Consumers who may be eligible for refunds can contact the Consumers Association of Singapore.

data.title: Middle East conflict tops risk list in September, MAS says
data.description:
A bursting of the “AI bubble" was the second most-cited downside risk.

Escalating conflict in the Middle East, flagged by 70.6% of respondents in a MAS survey, remain the top-cited risk to Singapore's economic outlook in September.

Nearly half of respondents, 47.1%, named it their single biggest concern, well ahead of any other downside risk.

A bursting of the "Artificial intelligence bubble" was the second most-cited downside risk, rising to 64.7% with 29.4% ranking it their top worry. 

Other geopolitical tensions, including trade tensions, were cited by 41.2%, up from 35.0%.

On the upside, a de-escalation of the Middle East conflict was cited by 35.5% of respondents, down sharply from 55% in June, and was not ranked as anyone's top upside risk.

All respondents instead identified a sustained AI-driven upturn in the technology cycle as the top upside support, unanimous in both the June and September surveys.

The risk backdrop comes even as forecasters sharply upgraded their growth outlook. The Singapore economy expanded 5.9% year on year in the second quarter, prompting respondents to raise their full-year 2026 GDP forecast to 5% from 3.5%.

Manufacturing, wholesale and retail trade, and non-oil domestic exports saw the largest sector upgrades, with exports revised to 17% growth from 6.1%.

data.title: Over half of employers to moderate or freeze wages in 2027: SNEF survey
data.description:
Rising manpower costs remain employers' top manpower challenge.

More than half of employers in Singapore (51%) plan to implement wage moderation or a wage freeze in 2027, up from 48% in 2026, according to The Singapore National Employers Federation (SNEF)'s Survey on Wage and Employment Outlook 2026/2027.

The findings point to continued caution in employers' wage outlook, particularly amongst small and medium-sized enterprises, even as business expectations show signs of improvement.

The proportion of employers expecting uncertain business prospects in 2027 fell to 63% from 72% in 2026.

At the same time, 65% of companies expect to perform well in 2026, compared with 63% in 2025.

On hiring, 54% of employers said they are not planning to increase headcount, whilst 40% intend to hire more workers.

The remaining 6% plan to reduce headcount.

Amongst companies employing lower-wage workers, 86% said they remain committed to providing built-in wage increases in 2027, down from 96% in 2026.

The remaining 14% plan a wage freeze, whilst none of the employers surveyed intends to implement wage cuts in 2027.

Rising manpower costs remained the top manpower challenge, cited by 83% of employers in 2026, up from 79% in 2025.

Concerns over the rising cost of upskilling and reskilling workers also increased to 30% from 23%.

However, labour market tightness eased compared with a year earlier.

The proportion of employers reporting difficulties in attracting and retaining professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) fell to 41% from 47%, whilst those citing a shortage of local high-skilled talent declined to 35% from 42%.

Despite easing labour market pressures, attracting suitable talent remained employers' top human resources priority at 59%.

More employers also identified the exploration, adoption, and enhancement of artificial intelligence as a priority, rising to 48% in 2027 from 39% in 2026, alongside efforts to upskill and reskill employees.

The survey was conducted between June and August 2026 and gathered responses from more than 300 companies employing close to 160,000 workers across 20 industries, representing a mix of small, medium-sized and large enterprises.

data.title: Singapore captures 82.5% of blockchain funding in Southeast Asia
data.description:
The city-state hosts 2,285 of the 3,957 blockchain companies tracked by Tracxn.

Singapore accounted for 82.5% of all-time blockchain equity funding tracked across Southeast Asia, according to a report by private-market data platform Tracxn.

The city-state was also home to 2,285 of the 3,957 blockchain companies identified in the region, representing approximately 58% of the total.

The figures place Singapore well ahead of the other blockchain hubs covered by Tracxn and show that regional capital and company formation remain heavily concentrated in the city-state.

Singapore’s ecosystem includes businesses operating across crypto financial services, digital-asset platforms, blockchain networks and decentralised-application development.

Tracxn also identified SBI Group’s acquisition of Singapore-based cryptocurrency platform CoinHako as one of the region’s notable blockchain transactions in 2026.

data.title: Maybank keeps Singtel at buy on credible FY2030 roadmap
data.description:
Optus’s recovery, NCS growth and AI data-centre demand underpin the unchanged $5.21 target.

Maybank maintained its buy rating and $5.21 target price for Singtel, citing potential earnings growth from Optus, NCS and its digital infrastructure business.

The target implies an estimated total return of approximately 20%, including dividends, based on Singtel’s $4.51 share price at the time of the report.

Maybank said Singtel’s roadmap to increase operating-company EBIT to between $2.1b and $2.5b by FY2030 appeared credible. Operating-company EBIT currently stands at approximately $1.5b.

The research house expects Optus’s recovery to be one of the main drivers. It estimated that moving towards an EBITDA margin of approximately 33% by FY2030 could contribute about $500m in additional EBIT.

NCS is also showing improved operating leverage, with EBIT rising 29% year on year in 1QFY2027. Maybank expects artificial intelligence to support productivity and create new revenue opportunities for the business.

Digital InfraCo could provide further upside through growing demand for AI infrastructure.

Singtel’s RE business has contracted 6 megawatts of capacity, with another 6 megawatts under advanced negotiation and 6 megawatts reserved. This provides visibility over a potential 18-megawatt footprint.

Maybank said Singapore’s sovereign AI demand could reach approximately 50 to 75 megawatts over three years. RE deployments are also customer-underwritten, with upfront payments of between 25% and 35%, reducing inventory risk.

The research house forecasts Singtel’s core net profit to rise from $2.77b in FY2026 to $3.09b in FY2027 and $3.58b in FY2028.

data.title: Daily Markets Briefing: STI up 0.06%; Top stock is DFI Retail
data.description:
DFI Retail is the top stock with a 3.41% increase.

The Straits Times Index (STI) closed at 5,747.710, up 0.06% on 3 September, at 5:21 p.m.

DFI Retail Group was the most active stock, followed by Hongkong Land (+1.97%) and Sembcorp Industries (+1.48%).

Mapletree Pan Asia Commercial Trust and UOL Group Limited were at the foot.

data.title: Singapore Business Review Technology Enterprise Summit 2026: Turning AI ambition into enterprise value
data.description:
Case studies on enterprise AI ROI take centre stage on 12 November in Singapore.

Most enterprises have already run their AI pilots. The Singapore Business Review Technology Enterprise Summit 2026, organised by Singapore Business Review, takes on what comes next — on 12 November at the Grand Copthorne Waterfront Hotel in Singapore, under the theme "AI at Scale: Proving Enterprise Value."

This case-study-led summit brings together leaders from technology, marketing, sales, customer experience, finance, logistics, and operations to examine how enterprises are converting AI investment into measurable growth, productivity, and resilience. Topics include AI governance, agentic systems, data readiness, workforce transformation, predictive decision-making, intelligent operations, customer engagement, and measuring ROI on AI.

Panel discussions are structured around the decisions enterprises face when scaling beyond the proof-of-concept stage. Sessions will cover leading the AI enterprise, scaling agentic AI with trust and governance, connecting marketing, sales, technology and customer experience, and redesigning operating models for AI readiness.

Confirmed speakers include Luc Grimond, managing director and senior partner at Boston Consulting Group; Kelvin Wong, chief technology officer, SASPAC Group digital chief information officer and head of ATSG at KPMG; Keith Leong, chief customer officer for enterprise at Singtel Singapore; Jayant Raman, head of AI partnerships for Asia Pacific at Oliver Wyman; Roy Wee, head of digital products and services at IHH Healthcare Singapore; James Fong, senior vice president of enterprise digital ecosystem and business at Changi Airport Group; and Varun Sharma, APAC head of data and analytics at HEINEKEN Asia Pacific.

The summit also offers an opportunity to connect with peers across industries navigating the same AI scaling challenges.

The summit runs from 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM at the Waterfront Ballroom, Level 2, Grand Copthorne Waterfront Hotel Singapore.

Companies interested in sponsoring the event may reach out to [email protected].

For more information, visit the Singapore Business Review Technology Enterprise Summit 2026's official website. To register, click here. For inquiries, contact [email protected].
